parsed.main_gap: The proof that at least one non-unit always remains rests on a false general principle (a non-increasing positive integer sequence 'can never reach 0'); the true reason (a move needs two non-units and yields at least one) is not given.

errors.description: Invalid justification that K ≥ 1 always. A non-increasing positive integer can certainly reach 0. The correct argument (each move requires two non-units and produces lcm(m,n)>1, so K drops by at most 1 and moves stop at K=1; or G_p ≥ 1 for a prime dividing A_1) is missing, though easily supplied.
errors.quote:
A nonnegative integer that
never increases and starts at a positive value can never reach \(0\); hence \(K\ge1\) at
every stage

parsed.notes: Termination via lexicographic (P,K) descent and the prime-wise Euclidean gcd invariant are both correct and well presented; the closed form M = ∏ p^{gcd of valuations} is right. Only the non-vanishing-of-K step is unsound but trivially repairable.
